Uses and Administration Glibenclamide is a sulfonylurea antidiabetic (p.460). It is given orally in the treatment of type 2 diabetes mel- litus (p.431) and has a duration of action of up to 24 hours. The usual initial dose of conventional formulations in type 2 diabetes mellitus is 2.5 to 5 mg daily with break- fast, adjusted every 7 days in steps of 2.5 or 5 mg daily up to 15 mg daily. Although increasing the dose above 15 mg is unlikely to produce further benefit, doses of up to 20 mg daily have been given. Doses greater than 10 mg daily may be given in 2 divided doses. Because of the relatively long duration of action of glibencla- mide, it is best avoided in the elderly. In some countries micronised preparations of gliben- clamide are available, in which the drug is formulated with a smaller particle size, and which have enhanced bioavailability. The usual initial dose of one such prep- aration (Glynase PresTab; Pharmacia Upjohn, USA) is 1.5 to 3 mg daily, adjusted every 7 days in steps of 1.5 mg, up to a usual maximum of 12 mg daily. Doses greater than 6 mg daily may be given in 2 divided dos- es. Action. Proceedings of a symposium on the mechanism of ac- tion of glibenclamide.1 1. Gavin JR, ed.
